name: Beryllium chloride
description: Beryllium chloride (CAS 7787-47-5 ) is an inorganic salt used primarily as a catalyst and precursor in specialized chemical synthesis. BeCl2 serves as a key entry point for producing high-purity beryllium metal. This compound is essential for beryllium-based materials required across advanced industrial sectors. In electronics and semiconductor manufacturing, it acts as a precursor for depositing beryllium oxide coatings. These coatings are valued for their thermal management performance in high-power components. Aerospace and defense applications rely on it as a starting material for producing beryllium metal used in structural alloys. It is also utilized in gyroscopes and guidance systems. In metallurgical processing, it functions as a flux and alloying agent precursor for copper-beryllium alloys, which are specified for precision tooling. Organic synthesis operations also employ this chemical as a Lewis acid catalyst in select Friedel-Crafts and related reactions. It is often chosen where conventional catalysts are unsuitable for the process. The product is supplied as an anhydrous crystalline solid, with anhydrous purity being the standard commercial form. This is due to the compound's high reactivity with moisture during storage and handling. Technical and high-purity research grades are available, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99.9%+. Packaging is handled under strict containment protocols given regulatory controls on beryllium. These safety measures are standard in most markets to ensure safe transport and delivery.
